milestones.title: Product Definition Review
milestones.purpose: Review whether the current bounded product-shaping choices are mature enough to count as a coherent product-definition front.
milestones.required_grounding: Grounded bounded decision fronts with explicit review questions.
milestones.required_readiness: At least one bounded decision should be close enough to review without pretending the overall product is settled.
missing_evidence: Current cost posture is `product_tier_mismatch_risk` / `target_tier_mismatch`, so product definition should stay prototype-scoped rather than reading as a `discreet_consumer_assistive_wearable` product path.
review_questions: What confidence format should V1 use by default during live subtitle support?
What should the default subtitle position behavior be for V1 live use?
What bounded memory/cache default should V1 use before richer recall behavior is expanded?
milestones.why_not_ready_yet: Current cost posture is `product_tier_mismatch_risk` / `target_tier_mismatch`, so product definition should stay prototype-scoped rather than reading as a `discreet_consumer_assistive_wearable` product path.

milestones.title: Prototype Viability Review
milestones.purpose: Review whether the current project can honestly sustain a viable prototype path rather than only abstract design motion.
milestones.required_grounding: Prototype viability requires current-truth subsystem context plus a bounded product-definition front.
milestones.required_readiness: Blocked and held lanes should be visible and limited enough that viability review is meaningful.
blocking_factors: Capture concrete link-latency or reconnect evidence from the phone-first path before reopening boundary changes.
Ground firmware readiness in explicit touch-input and display-control behavior instead of inferring it from project intent.
Ground trust-preserving recall with confidence objects and reinforcement rules before expanding cache policy or retention scope.
missing_evidence: too many active blockers remain for a credible viability review
Prototype viability can still be worth reviewing, but it must not be mistaken for consumer-tier product viability under the current cost posture.
review_questions: What is the highest-risk blocker still preventing a credible prototype viability claim?

milestones.required_grounding: Multiple subsystems should be grounded or at least weakly grounded under current-truth scorecard context.
milestones.required_readiness: Subsystem readiness should be strong enough to review without hiding limited-evidence lanes.
blocking_factors: Capture concrete link-latency or reconnect evidence from the phone-first path before reopening boundary changes.
Ground firmware readiness in explicit touch-input and display-control behavior instead of inferring it from project intent.
Ground trust-preserving recall with confidence objects and reinforcement rules before expanding cache policy or retention scope.
review_questions: What would materially ground Wireless Interface next?
What would materially ground Firmware next?
What would materially ground Memory System next?

milestones.title: Implementation Package Review
milestones.purpose: Review whether the current implementation-artifact package is mature enough to inspect as a bounded package rather than scattered review fragments.
milestones.required_grounding: Draft-emission readiness and emitted review artifacts should both be grounded enough to inspect together.
milestones.required_readiness: At least one emitted or strongly draft-ready artifact should exist before package review becomes real.
missing_evidence: Implementation-package review can stay live for prototype buildability, but current cost posture `product_tier_mismatch_risk` blocks reading it as a `discreet_consumer_assistive_wearable` implementation package.
review_questions: Which parts of this implementation package are still prototype-learning scaffolds and should not be read as consumer-product commitments?

milestones.title: Product Realism Check
milestones.purpose: Review whether current evidence justifies anything stronger than prototype-level claims, in line with the declared project seriousness.
milestones.required_grounding: A stronger product claim needs grounded runtime, trust, and subsystem evidence beyond report-only plausibility.
milestones.required_readiness: Realism review should only move forward when the project is actually aiming at a product-candidate or real-product path.
blocking_factors: Capture concrete link-latency or reconnect evidence from the phone-first path before reopening boundary changes.
Ground firmware readiness in explicit touch-input and display-control behavior instead of inferring it from project intent.
Ground trust-preserving recall with confidence objects and reinforcement rules before expanding cache policy or retention scope.

Current cost posture is `product_tier_mismatch_risk` with signal `stop_if_cost_target_matters`, so stronger product realism should stay capped until the `discreet_consumer_assistive_wearable` cost story is reframed or materially improved.
missing_evidence: core runtime behavior is grounded beyond report-only reasoning
trust, privacy, and usability constraints are handled credibly enough to survive real use
important subsystem risks are no longer being hidden behind prototype-only excuses
Prototype-learning value may still be real, but product-facing realism should not advance while economic posture is mismatched.
review_questions: What would have to become true before a stronger product claim would be honest?
milestones.why_not_ready_yet: Current operator expectations do not yet target a real product claim, so realism review should stay held rather than being forced early.
